en: Gallium is a solid metal at room temperature but melts into a liquid when held in your bare hand.
The Statue of Liberty is green because its copper surface underwent a chemical change, reacting with air to form copper carbonate.
Oobleck, a mixture of cornstarch and water, acts like a solid when punched but flows like a liquid when poured.
Unlike most substances, water expands when freezing, making solid ice less dense than liquid water so it floats.
The Sun and stars are made of plasma, a superheated state of matter where electrons separate from their atoms.
Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide that undergoes sublimation, skipping the liquid phase to become a cold gas at room temperature.
Milk is an emulsion, a mixture where tiny droplets of liquid fat are suspended throughout mostly liquid water.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar causes a chemical change producing carbon dioxide gas, creating fizzy bubbles in volcano experiments.
Water molecules stick together through cohesion, creating surface tension that allows water striders to walk across ponds without sinking.
Gold is highly malleable, meaning one gram can be hammered into a one-square-meter sheet without breaking or cracking.
Heating white sugar causes caramelization, a chemical change breaking down molecules to create new compounds giving brown caramel its flavor.
A supersaturated solution forms when hot water dissolves more sugar than normally possible, creating rock candy crystals as it cools.
